centralThesis.text: Tool discovery gives an Agent a callable schema, but it does not grant execution permission.

audienceValue.viewerNeed: Understand one concrete Agent runtime behavior rather than memorize an architecture diagram.
audienceValue.promisedTakeaway: Recognize the exact state change from no registered tool to a schema-valid call, and its permission boundary.

mechanism.inputState: The runtime has no registered tool schema.
mechanism.transformation: A discovery response supplies the tool name, description, and input schema, which the runtime registers.
mechanism.outputState: The model can construct a schema-valid call, while the permission gate still controls execution.

proofObjects.description: A source-supported discovery response containing name, description, and inputSchema.

claims.text: Tool discovery changes the runtime from having no callable schema to having one registered schema.

definitions.explanation: The structured argument contract used to construct and validate a tool call.

relationships.explanation: The runtime registers returned metadata before the model constructs a valid call.

limitations.text: Discovery and schema validity do not bypass runtime permission checks.
